before: Nominal seasonal catch per tow-hour for herring, sablefish, Chinook salmon, chum salmon, and pollock in available EBS pollock-dominated haul records, 1991-2026, with source vessel types 1-3 combined. Each rate is the sum of available extrapolated catch divided by the sum of positive valid haul hours in the same year and season; the calculation uses the ratio of totals. Weight rates are kg per tow-hour for herring and sablefish and tons per tow-hour for pollock. Salmon rates are extrapolated fish per tow-hour. A season is January-May and B season is June-December, retaining the original figure’s calendar split. Selection requires NMFS area 500-539, positive official total catch, and pollock kg / official total catch in tons >800 (a >80% pollock proxy). 2026 values are preliminary; B-season records extend through September 18, 2026 and are partial. Historical years use their full available seasons. Blank species entries are omitted from available catch sums, retained in the effort denominator, and counted in the plotting table. Entirely unreported species-season combinations are gaps, including sablefish in 2014. The file has incomplete CV/EM coverage; no CV records pass the target filter in 2025-2026. Rates describe the available source records; fleet-wide catch accounting uses a separate dataset.
after: Nominal seasonal catch per tow-hour for herring, sablefish, Chinook salmon, chum salmon, and pollock in EBS pollock-dominated hauls, 1991–2026. Rates equal total extrapolated catch divided by total valid tow-hours. Units are kg per tow-hour for herring and sablefish, tons per tow-hour for pollock, and fish per tow-hour for salmon. A season is January–May; B season is June–December. Hauls are in NMFS areas 500–539, with positive total catch and more than 80% pollock by weight. The 2026 B-season data extend through September 18. Missing species catches are omitted from catch sums while their tow-hours remain in the denominator; unreported species-season combinations appear as gaps. Catcher-vessel and electronic-monitoring coverage is incomplete; catcher-vessel records are absent in 2025–2026 after filtering.

before: Estimated EBS pollock catch numbers (thousands of fish) by sex for the A season (January-May), B season (June-December), and annual total, 1991-2025. Circles denote females and triangles denote males. B-season estimates combine the northwest and southeast strata, and annual totals equal A+B. Shading marks provisional 2024-2025 estimates on the original sampler age basis.
after: Estimated EBS pollock catch numbers (thousands of fish) by sex for the A season (January–May), B season (June–December), and annual total, 1991–2025. Circles denote females and triangles denote males. B-season estimates combine northwest and southeast areas; annual totals equal A + B. Shading marks provisional 2024–2025 estimates based on released FT-NIRS ages before conversion to thin-section tester ages. Both years cover all 12 months. The estimates have limited age–length coverage: approximately 0.50% and 0.36% of catch biomass, respectively, remain unallocated in unsupported cells.

before: Cumulative EBS pollock catch as a proportion of annual specified TAC for weeks ending in January, February, March, and April, 2000–2026. Catch includes retained and discarded pollock from all gears and targets in the Bering Sea subarea, excluding Bogoslof reporting area 518. Each full reporting week is assigned to its week-ending month. The denominator is the annual stock TAC from harvest specifications, before later AI-to-BS quota transfers. Amendment 110 shifted five percentage points of the directed fishery seasonal allocation from B to A to provide greater flexibility to avoid Chinook salmon bycatch; 2017 was the first A season after the rule took effect.
after: Cumulative EBS pollock catch as a proportion of annual specified TAC for weeks ending in January, February, March, and April, 2000–2026. Each full reporting week is assigned to its week-ending month. The denominator is the annual stock TAC from harvest specifications, before later AI-to-BS quota transfers. Amendment 110 shifted five percentage points of the directed fishery seasonal allocation from B to A to provide greater flexibility to avoid Chinook salmon bycatch; 2017 was the first A season after the rule took effect.

before: Fleet dispersion in the A and B seasons, 2000–2026 using a daily pairwise-distance approach. Unique tow pairs are formed within each day and vessel group (catcher-processors and observed catcher vessels); seasonal means pool distance sums and pair counts across both groups. No cross-group pairs are included. Distances are great-circle nautical miles. Solid lines use available seasonal records; dashed lines use records occurring between January 1 and September 18. The 2026 B season is partial. Tows included caught more than 80% pollock by catch weight, had valid locations, occurred in EBS reporting areas 500–539, and had tow durations between zero and 40 hours. Duration is calculated from timestamps with recorded minutes as fallback. Electronic-monitoring catcher-vessel records are absent.

before: Model 26.0 spawning exploitation for spawning-to-spawning intervals starting in 1964–2026. Black lines show the revised production fit; dashed blue lines and shading show MCMC posterior medians and central 95% credible intervals from 5,000 existing draws. Each within-draw ratio compares next-spawning biomass with and without fishing from a shared spawning-date population. The terminal interval assumes 1.375 million t catch in 2027, within-draw mean 1978–2023 recruitment and mean 2023–2025 selectivity, and the revised deterministic fishery-weight schedule. Biology is fixed. The terminal posterior median is 14.5333%, with interval 11.2075–18.3700%.
after: Model 26.0 spawning exploitation for spawning-to-spawning intervals starting in 1964–2026. Black lines show the Model 26.0 fit; dashed blue lines and shading show MCMC posterior medians and central 95% credible intervals from 5,000 draws. Each within-draw ratio compares next-spawning biomass with and without fishing from a shared spawning-date population. The terminal interval assumes 1.375 million t catch in 2027, within-draw mean 1978–2023 recruitment and mean 2023–2025 selectivity, and the deterministic fishery-weight schedule. Biology is fixed. The terminal posterior median is 14.5333%, with interval 11.2075–18.3700%.

before: Observed indices and Model 26.0 fitted predictions. Black points show source observations, lines show fitted predictions, and bars show approximate 95% observation-error ranges. before: ATS-q negative log marginal density and likelihood profile for Model 26.0. The marginal density uses a kernel estimate from all 5,000 saved draws; equal-grid probabilities also sum to one. Panel B pairs weighted quadratic regressions fitted directly to all 5,000 MCMC component values with profile NLL contributions for composition data, index data and selectivity deviates. The smoothers use individual draws and are displayed over the central 99% of sampled ATS q. MCMC curves are centered at the ATS-q marginal mode; profile components retain the profile minimum as their reference. These smoothers describe conditional mean native objective components; the negative log marginal density has no unique additive decomposition into those components. Other is omitted.

before: Index checks compare observed survey and historical catch-rate indices with simulated observations generated from 1,000 MCMC draws. Each draw supplies a model expectation; random observation errors are then added using the same error assumptions used to fit each index, including the relationships among BTS errors. Lines show median expectations and shading covers the middle 95% of simulated observations at each year. Circles are observed indices and triangles identify existing substitutes. Some simulated values are negative because the fitted Normal error distributions allow them. The BTS overall mismatch measure exceeds its observed value in 0.2% of simulations, indicating that the model rarely reproduces this feature of the BTS data. Units differ among panels. Biological inputs remain fixed.
after: Index checks compare observed survey and historical catch-rate indices with simulated observations generated from 1,000 MCMC draws. Some simulated values are negative because the fitted Normal error distributions allow them. The BTS overall mismatch measure exceeds its observed value in 0.2% of simulations, indicating that the model rarely reproduces this feature of the BTS data. Biological inputs remain fixed.

before: Age-composition checks compare the latest three observed samples from each data source with simulated samples generated from 1,000 MCMC draws. Lines show median model proportions, shading covers the middle 95% of simulated sample proportions at each age, and points show observed proportions. The shading includes parameter uncertainty and the assumed sampling variation. This simulation approximates the age-composition fitting formula, which adds a small constant to age proportions when calculating fit. The 2020 ATS substitute is excluded. Age 15 includes all older fish. Age conversions, weights and other biology remain fixed.
